#!/bin/bash

# Flux directives translated from SLURM
#FLUX: -q gpu
#FLUX: -g 1
#FLUX: -N 1
#FLUX: -n 1
#FLUX: -t 01:30:00
#FLUX: -o with_gpu.out

#
# --- Omitted SLURM options and explanations ---
#
# --gres-flags=enforce-binding
#   Omitted. This is a SLURM-specific flag related to how GPUs are bound to CPUs.
#   Flux has its own binding mechanisms which are generally handled automatically.
#   Performance implication: If the default binding provided by Flux is not
#   optimal for this application, performance could be degraded due to NUMA
#   effects or other affinity issues.
#
# -e with_gpu.err
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into the single output file
#   specified by the -o directive. To redirect stderr separately, you can use
#   shell redirection in your command, e.g., 'command 2> with_gpu.err'.
#
# Note on memory:
#   The original SLURM script did not request a specific amount of memory. This
#   job will receive the default memory allocation from the scheduler, which could
#   be insufficient for a GPU job and lead to an out-of-memory error.
#

# Load CUDA module
module load cuda/12.2.2  gcc/10.2   


nvidia-smi 

# Compile CUDA program and run
#nvcc -arch sm_20 vecadd.cu -o vecadd
nvcc -O2 -std=c++11 hw4.cu -o a.out
nvprof ./a.out
nsys profile ./a.out

issues: As correctly noted in the script's comments, the original SLURM memory request was omitted. This is a significant omission. Without a memory constraint, the job is at risk of being scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, leading to an out-of-memory failure.

The omission of `--gres-flags=enforce-binding` is also a potential performance issue. If the application is sensitive to CPU-GPU affinity (e.g., due to NUMA effects), the default binding provided by Flux may be sub-optimal, leading to lower performance.

Including compilation (`nvcc`) in a batch script is generally poor practice. Code should be compiled before job submission to separate the build and execution phases and to avoid wasting compute-node time on compilation.
The script executes `./a.out` using a relative path, which requires the job to be submitted from the directory containing the source file (`hw4.cu`). This can be a fragile practice.

#!/bin/bash
#!/bin/bash

# Request a GPU partition node and access to 1 GPU
#SBATCH -p gpu --gres=gpu:1 --gres-flags=enforce-binding

# Ensures all allocated cores are on the same node
#SBATCH -N 1

# Request 1 CPU core
#SBATCH -n 1

#SBATCH -t 01:30:00
#SBATCH -o with_gpu.out
#SBATCH -e with_gpu.err

# Load CUDA module
module load cuda/12.2.2  gcc/10.2   


nvidia-smi 

# Compile CUDA program and run
#nvcc -arch sm_20 vecadd.cu -o vecadd
nvcc -O2 -std=c++11 hw4.cu -o a.out
nvprof ./a.out
nsys profile ./a.out
